findings.explanation: The root-to-raw-data link leads to an ancestral submodule whose URL is an absolute filesystem path. Partial is defensible for the expressly recursive component scope; this does not establish that published processed inputs cannot be used. The word private is not supported by a filesystem URL alone.
findings.suggested_correction: Replace private with host-local; distinguish ancestral-source regeneration from the inputs consumed by the root analysis.

findings.explanation: The immediate input links and recorded input selectors stay under the root, but recursively following raw_eyegaze exposes the nonportable lab-eyetracking link. Partial correctly preserves that known structural defect without converting absent downloads into retrieval failures.

The delivered Docker recipe includes the scientific and rendering distributions, and the Make target installs the separately pinned REMoDNaV source. This satisfies inclusion under the native equivalent-evidence rule; precision of versions is a separate question.

The frozen inventory and history establish Git tracking for the study sources and configuration. Omitted source-capture payloads cannot be interpreted as untracked original delivery changes; the override and mapping warning are justified.

Large container layers have explicit sizes and annex identities; the data datasets also expose annex-managed content. This supports use of an appropriate large-content VCS. The review does not establish size or storage appropriateness of every ordinary Git binary in the benchmark module.

The inspected root run records exit zero, image extra_input, declared results and input selectors. The linked label run records the host-shell command and outputs but carries no actual environment identity. Partial correctly distinguishes real provenance from complete environment provenance.

The current README gives installation prerequisites, cloning, a named rerun and manuscript building. It explicitly labels the obsolete root instructions and discloses changed results, so their coexistence does not trigger the silent-conflict rule for this root entry point.

The named rerun reaches an actual recorded action, whose Make target calls the analysis with result and figure switches. This is a clear starting point, independent of whether a new recipient can currently retrieve all payloads.

The linked submit generators really embed a user-specific working directory and fixed Python path. Their presence supports a partial finding for the included component, while image-internal cleanup paths do not constitute host-path defects. The reason correctly calls the submitters legacy.

The cited pandas/seaborn omission does not establish dependency incompleteness on the declared or recorded generation route. Both packages are in the root Dockerfile; the actual linked label action calls REMoDNaV, whose linked setup.py declares numpy, scipy, statsmodels and matplotlib. The cited plotting script is not called by that action. A separate specification in every module is not required by the native equivalent-evidence rule.
findings.suggested_correction: Re-evaluate completeness using the actual root and linked-generation commands and their linked package specifications. Either identify a concrete undeclared requirement on an in-scope route or change this finding to met for those routes. Preserve the missing historical environment identity under must/006 and must/015.

findings.explanation: The root names major host tools, but the linked Condor route imports host environment and assumes a particular executable and working directory without setup instructions. The captured adapter additionally assumes non-root Docker access. These are concrete undisclosed host prerequisites, so partial is supported.

Requirements for the current root route are explicit. The linked module README instead instructs readers to submit jobs using deleted Python programs and omits a usable setup for the retained generator. Partial reflects a genuine documentation gap rather than merely missing exact pins.

The existing environment and package specifications are tracked with code and module pins. This criterion concerns version control of specifications; it need not duplicate the separate shortcomings in historical identity or setup documentation.

The history supplies a runnable build declaration followed by an executed build/save record and later executed archive conversion. This meets the instrument-specific command-plus-history interpretation, beyond mere initial file creation. The duplicate flag is correct. The ENV-change message was inspected but its patch was unavailable without lazy fetching.

The archived image has content digests; the inspected adapter hashes its config and runs the image identity, so latest is not sufficient evidence of a floating registry environment here. The label-generation run still lacks an exact recorded environment, supporting partial across the scope.

Native rules require recipient verification, which this cohort prohibits. Location claims and source recipes cannot establish current retrieval of image/data bytes. Not-checked is the appropriate outcome, and no observed download failure is asserted.

Root environment use is documented. Following the linked label README instead reaches nonexistent Python scripts and misses the retained generator; generated submit files are not themselves the key defect. Partial is supported by the mismatch between delivered code and that module documentation.

The independently linked components use Git trees and gitlinks, with DataLad/annex layered on the same version-control family for datasets. No competing component VCS is evidenced in the inspected boundary.

A past successful study run and a linked software test definition do not establish regular validation of the study instructions. Not-checked avoids the erroneous inference that no study CI file proves no testing.

Raw data, derived labels and algorithm code have distinct pinned component boundaries; the root separates environment, analysis source and generated outputs. The separation is concrete and does not depend on arbitrary updates having been tested.

A completed historical result-generating container invocation, together with the adapter implementation of docker run --rm, meets the instrument allowance for equivalent completed fresh-run evidence. It proves neither a current replay nor scientific validity, and the assessment explicitly avoids those claims.

The root route does create disposable Docker instances. However the same assessment includes linked label generation when judging provenance and portability, and that recorded route executes host Python through PYTHONPATH without creating or disposing an environment. The blanket met therefore narrows the boundary only for this positive.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the declared recursive computational scope: disposable root computation, host-environment label generation. Alternatively justify a consistently narrower execution boundary across all affected criteria.

findings.explanation: The history provides creation and later format maintenance, including an exit-zero conversion. These do not establish regular reconstitution tests of the exact scientific environments. Not-checked preserves this evidential distinction.

Image paths and content identities are part of the research object rather than only registry tags. Absence of the actual layers from this inspection capture limits retrieval checks, not the demonstrated archiving mechanism.

The same runnable build and recorded maintenance evidence supporting must/014 supports this duplicate. The matching verdict and explicit upstream-duplicate flag avoid presenting it as an independent substantive check.

The public dataset declaration does not resolve the access conditions of the uninspected ancestral source. A host-local URL alone proves neither restriction nor public access. Not-checked is reasonable for the recursive scope; the ancestor already has its own module boundary, but its access status remains unknown.

This object has independently maintained datasets and code components, so the criterion is applicable. Most are identified by gitlinks and public URLs; the nested lab source URL is nonportable. Partial correctly avoids confusing ordinary Python package dependencies with project modules.

The root documents the broad dataset/container route, but the linked label instructions neither explain its present generator nor connect its independently pinned algorithm to the root algorithm. The incomplete explanation of recombination supports partial.

Read-only Git tree inspection confirms distinct root and label REMoDNaV gitlinks, at d289118 and c9b8696 respectively. Adoption can therefore be controlled independently. This supports boundary isolation, not compatibility of arbitrary replacements.
findings.suggested_correction: Cite the pinned trees alongside .gitmodules when asserting exact gitlink revisions; .gitmodules itself contains paths and URLs, not those commit IDs.

findings.explanation: The run selectors explicitly connect module inputs to root results, and the registration connects the archived image to Make. This is an actual composition mechanism, despite incomplete documentation of some linked components.

Gitlinks and root DataLad instructions provide navigation tooling, but the linked module README directs users away from the delivered generator. Partial captures useful existing navigation plus a concrete documentation failure.

limitations: Inspection-only review of the assigned anonymized native JSON, pinned instrument, and explicitly linked frozen source corpus. No peer assessments or reviews were consulted. Agreement is not human approval.

No network, payload acquisition, image build or scientific workflow execution occurred. Missing annex/binary payloads are capture omissions, not observed retrieval failures; numerical agreement and scientific adequacy remain untested.

The manifest SHA256 and all downloaded source-file hashes were checked. The native checklist pin check and response validator passed, but substantive judgments were evaluated independently. Counts in the supplied JSON are 17 MUST (7 met, 9 partial, 1 not-checked), 9 SHOULD (6 met, 3 not-checked), and 5 MAY (2 met, 3 partial); no scalar score or inconsistent stored denominator is present. No separate report was supplied for review.

All Git reads used GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. The c531a59 commit read and the 92dbad28 Dockerfile patch encountered omitted-object limitations; c531a59 was inspected through the frozen history text, and the 92dbad28 patch remains unverified. No fetch was attempted.

The original assessor probe receipt was not part of the assigned input. Probe-attributed conclusions were checked against source evidence, not against an unseen execution receipt. The external adapter was inspected from its manifest-hashed capture; no current package installation or behavior was tested.
